$comment: Single source of truth for every inference option. Read by:
desktop/renderer/src/lib/specs.ts      -> defaults, field metadata, tune grids
desktop/args.js                         -> CLI flag list for buildArgs
Adding an option here should mean editing nothing else.
label/tip are the desktop app's wording; cliHelp is the terminal's. They
are allowed to read differently because they are different audiences.

model.label: Model
model.tip: The voice you want to sound like. Pick one before you go live.
model.cliHelp: Path to a trained .pth voice model

index.label: Index
index.tip: An optional file that pulls the result closer to that voice. None turns this off.

indexRate.label: Index rate
indexRate.tip: How much the index file is used. 0 uses only the voice. 1 leans on the index as much as it can.

key.label: Pitch
key.tip: Moves your voice up or down. A higher number sounds higher. A lower number sounds lower. It stops at two octaves.

formant.label: Formant
formant.tip: Makes the voice brighter or darker without moving the note as much. 0 leaves the tone alone.

f0.label: Pitch tracker
f0.tip: How the app hears the note you are singing. RMVPE is the usual choice. FCPE uses less of the computer. PM is the older method.

f0Min.label: Lowest pitch (Hz)
f0Min.tip: The lowest tone counted as a voice. Anything lower is ignored.
f0Min.cliHelp: Lowest pitch treated as voiced, in Hz

f0Max.label: Highest pitch (Hz)
f0Max.tip: The highest tone counted as a voice. Keep it above the lowest pitch.

rmvpeThreshold.label: RMVPE threshold
rmvpeThreshold.tip: How sure the usual pitch method must be before it counts a note. A higher number ignores more noise.

fcpeThreshold.label: FCPE threshold
fcpeThreshold.tip: How sure the lighter pitch method must be before it counts a note. A higher number ignores more noise.

rmsMixRate.label: Loudness mix
rmsMixRate.tip: 0 follows how loud you are. 1 keeps the loudness of the chosen voice.

inputGain.label: Mic gain
inputGain.tip: Turns the microphone up or down before conversion. 1 leaves it as it is.
inputGain.cliHelp: Multiply the microphone or file before conversion

outputGain.label: Speaker gain
outputGain.tip: Turns the converted voice up or down. 1 leaves it as it is.

noClip.label: Don't clip
noClip.tip: Off keeps loud peaks inside a safe range. On leaves those peaks alone.
noClip.cliHelp: Leave samples outside -1..1 instead of clipping

blockTime.label: Block (seconds)
blockTime.tip: How much of your voice is converted at once. A smaller number answers faster and works the computer harder.

crossfadeTime.label: Crossfade (seconds)
crossfadeTime.tip: A short blend between each piece of audio so you do not hear clicks.

extraTime.label: Context (seconds)
extraTime.tip: How much of what you just said is kept in mind. More of it can sound steadier.

indexNeighbors.label: Index neighbors
indexNeighbors.tip: How many close matches from the index file are mixed together. Use a whole number, at least 1.
indexNeighbors.cliHelp: How many index vectors to blend

sampleRate.label: Sample rate
sampleRate.tip: How many samples play each second. 0 uses the voice model's own rate. Use a whole number.

inputChannels.label: Mic channels
inputChannels.tip: How many microphone channels to open. They are mixed into one voice. Use a whole number, at least 1.
inputChannels.cliHelp: Microphone channels to open, then mix to mono

outputChannels.label: Speaker channels
outputChannels.tip: How many speaker channels to play. The voice is copied onto each one. Use a whole number, at least 1.
outputChannels.cliHelp: Speaker channels. Mono audio is copied to each

latency.label: Latency
latency.tip: How long the sound card waits. Type low, high, or a number of seconds. Leave it empty to let the computer choose. This is separate from block time.
latency.cliHelp: low, high, or seconds. Default lets PortAudio choose

inputDevice.label: Microphone
inputDevice.tip: The microphone you speak into. System default follows the one Windows is using.
inputDevice.cliHelp: Microphone number or name. Default is the system input

outputDevice.label: Speakers
outputDevice.tip: Where the converted voice plays. System default uses your usual speakers.
outputDevice.cliHelp: Speaker number or name. Default is the system output

hostApi.label: Host API
hostApi.tip: Show devices from only one sound system, such as WASAPI. Leave it empty to allow every system.
hostApi.cliHelp: Only match devices on this PortAudio host, such as WASAPI

wasapiExclusive.label: WASAPI exclusive
wasapiExclusive.tip: Takes over the WASAPI microphone and speakers so other apps cannot share them. Both devices must be WASAPI.
wasapiExclusive.cliHelp: Open WASAPI devices in exclusive mode

wasapiAutoConvert.label: WASAPI resample
wasapiAutoConvert.tip: Lets WASAPI change the rate when a device does not match. Both the microphone and speakers must be WASAPI.
wasapiAutoConvert.cliHelp: Let WASAPI resample if the rate differs
